title: py-sdk incremental message router + resumable hook patterns for streaming chat
creator: Elena Kim
description:
Background: Customers integrating long-running chat UIs with the Python SDK frequently need small, well-defined primitives for: (1) routing incremental delta messages to multiple consumers, (2) checkpointing stream progress so UIs can resume after network hiccups, and (3) surfacing developer-friendly hooks for retries and idempotency. Current ad-hoc examples in examples/ are inconsistent and leak complexity (internal queues, raw SSE plumbing).

Goal: Ship a documented, ergonomic set of primitives in the Python SDK that: provide a single incremental-message router abstraction, a lightweight checkpoint/resume hook contract, and an example cookbook showing common patterns (retry on transient network errors, graceful backpressure, deduplication of tokens on resume). The API should be explicit about ordering guarantees, non-duplication when resume tokens are used, and traceable via telemetry events.

Non-goals: Implementing a distributed universal checkpoint store or a server-side guaranteed exactly-once delivery. Those can be follow-ups (ENG-xxxxx).
acceptance_criteria: New public API: MessageRouter and ResumeHook documented in sdk.chat.streaming (stable beta).
Example: 'resumable_chat_router.py' in examples/ that demonstrates resume after connection loss with a minimal UI harness (<= 200 LOC).
Server-visible telemetry events emitted for: stream.start, stream.resume, stream.fragment_received, stream.complete, stream.error (users can opt-in).

Behavior: ResumeHook accepts a checkpoint token string and returns a new object with last_processed_offset; calling MessageRouter.resume(checkpoint) continues from next token without duplicating already-delivered chunks.
Integration tests: unit tests and an e2e test against the local stream simulator that covers disconnect+resume and duplicate-chunk-suppression.
Docs: SDK reference doc + short cookbook with three patterns: (A) UI resume on flaky networks, (B) server-driven canary fallback on partial output, (C) bounded-queue backpressure to avoid OOM.
decision_log: 2026-02-20: Decided to keep API surface minimal: MessageRouter will be a single class with register/unregister consumer callbacks and an explicit resume() API rather than implicit checkpoint auto-retry. Rationale: simpler mental model and explicit developer control over duplicate suppression.
2026-02-22: Chose to use opaque checkpoint tokens (string) that encode (model, request_id, last_seq). Avoid introducing a pinned binary format to allow server-side evolution.
2026-02-24: Agreed that telemetry will be opt-in by default; users can enable via TelemetryConfig(enable_stream_events=True) to avoid PII concerns in default usage.
2026-03-01: Opted to emit 'fragment_id' (monotonic per-request) with each fragment to make deduplication in client trivial. Trade-off: extra metadata per fragment but much simpler resume semantics.
implementation_notes:
MessageRouter API sketch:
- constructor(socket_factory, loop=None, queue_maxsize=256)
- register_consumer(name:str, callback:Callable[[Fragment], Awaitable[None]]) -> token
- unregister_consumer(token)
- start() / stop()
- resume(checkpoint_token: str) -> None
- get_checkpoint() -> str  # opaque token to persist

ResumeHook contract:
- on_resume(checkpoint_token: str) -> ResumeContext(last_seq:int, dedupe_seen:Set[int])
- on_fragment(fragment) -> Accept|Skip decisions (consumer can implement idempotency)
Backpressure: use bounded asyncio.Queue per-consumer; if full, apply one of three policies (drop_oldest, drop_new, block). Default: drop_oldest and emit telemetry.warning. Document policy trade-offs.

Retries: networking retries (to re-establish SSE/WebSocket) will be handled by an outer retry loop with exponential backoff and jitter; MessageRouter.resume() should be idempotent so retries do not produce duplicates. Internal sequence numbers and fragment_id will be used to suppress already-processed fragments.

Edge-case: partial tokenization across fragments (server can chunk mid-token). We will provide a small helper 'ChunkRecomposer' for consumer examples to stitch tokens safely. It's included in examples/ not exported to top-level API now.
test_plan: Unit tests for MessageRouter: simulate fragment stream with simulated disconnects, assert consumer callbacks receive expected fragments and no duplicates after resume.
E2E test against 'stream-sim' fixture (tests/fixtures/stream-sim.py) that can serve reordered fragments and duplicate fragments to verify client dedupe logic.
Load test: micro-benchmark that exercises 100 concurrent lightweight consumers against a single router instance to verify queue_maxsize defaults and telemetry emissions.
Security: verify telemetry opt-out preserves no fragments in logs; run quick audit to ensure no PII output in telemetry event payloads.
rollout_plan: Feature branch: feature/py-resumable-router -> create PR and run CI (unit + linters).
Canary: publish beta wheel (rc) on pip under 'redwood-inference-sdk==0.42.0rc1' and ask two internal teams (Solutions Eng and Console) to validate using their staging workloads for one week.
Gradual: after validation, merge to main, publish GA wheel and add docs to docs.sdk.python/streaming.md. Monitor telemetry (opt-in) and incoming support channels for 72 hours.
Fallback: provide quick revert PR and a public 'how to disable' snippet if any unexpected consumer regressions appear.
